forecasts.reason: ~-5% time, ~-0.15pp vs true mean ~0.7555; lands near the 0.7545 line within 3-seed noise.
26px keeps the 3x3 final-map regime so accuracy ~unchanged; saves ~3-4% time (middle phase is ~30% of compute, 14% fewer pixels).
Small ramp change; a gain of 0.3pp or more on top of the final full copy is unlikely, so the effect is noise-level.
E013 showed label-smoothing changes are worth <0.1pp; a 0.2pp gain from per-phase LS is unlikely.
E021 recovered only half its MAC savings, implying sizeable non-conv or low-efficiency kernels; expect <90 TFLOP/s achieved.
Main step count matched to E017, so proxy forward/train is pure added cost; time rises rather than falling 5%.

cruxes: What is the tip's held-out 10-seed mean (seeds 3-12)? It sets the real margin over 0.753 and so how many epochs can be cut.
Does a 26px middle phase (3x3 final map) keep accuracy where 24px (2x2) lost 0.68pp? This separates the final-map-regime mechanism from plain pixel count.
What share of step time is non-conv (BN/GELU, pooling, Muon NS, Lookahead)? It caps the payoff of every width or depth lever.
structured_output.world_model: W5 after E021. Noise: rebuilds reshuffle results (E017 vs E019 on the same commit read 0.7537 vs 0.7541; commits with the same math span 0.7537-0.7607). Per-seed SD ~0.4pp, 3-seed SD ~0.25pp. True tip mean ~0.7555, so real margin ~0.25pp. Epoch dial ~2.3 s/pp is the best measured trade. Architecture cuts return less time than their MAC share (memory-bound elementwise work plus fixed costs). Low-res accuracy cost follows how many late steps run with a 3x3 final map: 32/28/26 px give 3x3 after group 3, 24/20 px give 2x2. So 26 px middle and 20 px early phases should be cheap in accuracy. Muon renormalizes filters, so filter wd is inert. Effective BN momentum is 0.4, so BN recalibration should add little. Proxy selection only pays if epochs are cut too.
